title: Tune for Retention, Not Just Gain: SFT Forgets Far Less than You Think
abstract: arXiv:2611.34579v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting, the drastic loss of previously acquired capabilities when learning new ones, is a central challenge in language model fine-tuning. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is widely believed to be prone to such forgetting. Recent works have attributed this to the off-policy nature of SFT, arguing that on-policy learning is key to continual learning. In this paper, we challenge this premise. We show that while maximizing new-task performance can induce catastrophic forgetting, alternative hyperparameter choices (lower learning rate and batch size) can yield similar gains with little to no forgetting. With hyperparameters selected jointly for gain and retention, vanilla SFT retains prior capabilities far better than previously suggested and can be competitive with Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT), an on-policy approach designed to mitigate forgetting. translated_title: 调优应以能力保持为目标，而非仅仅追求增益：SFT的遗忘远比你想象的少
translated_abstract: 灾难性遗忘，即在习得新能力时急剧丧失先前已获得的能力，是语言模型微调中的核心挑战。人们普遍认为监督微调（SFT）容易发生这种遗忘。近期研究将此归因于SFT的离策略（off-policy）特性，并认为在线策略学习是持续学习的关键。本文挑战了这一前提。我们证明，虽然最大化新任务性能确实会引发灾难性遗忘，但选择替代的超参数（更低的学习率和批量大小）可以在几乎不发生遗忘的情况下获得类似的新任务收益。当超参数的选择同时兼顾增益与能力保持时，普通SFT对既有能力的保持远好于此前的说法，并且可以与自蒸馏微调（SDFT）——一种旨在缓解遗忘的在线策略方法——相媲美。虽然SDFT对超参数选择可能更加鲁棒，但它也需要……（原文摘要截断于此）
tldr: 本文挑战了“SFT因其离策略特性而容易导致灾难性遗忘”的流行观点，证明通过选择更低学习率和批量大小等同时兼顾增益与能力保持的超参数，普通SFT对旧能力的保持远好于以往认知，甚至可与在线策略的SDFT方法相媲美。
